6:7: As, therefore, a cistern or pit makes its water cold, so in the midst of Jerusalem the wickedness that is in her has lost all the warmth of life. And this is to be noted, that the saints are called fervent in spirit, whereas evils are cold; whence that also is written, that in the last days, when iniquity has been multiplied, the love of many will grow cold. I think that this too means the same: I have been likened to those who go down into the pit. …
6:9: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Even to the last cluster they will glean, as in a vineyard, the remnant of Israel; turn back your hand like a grape-gatherer to the basket! LXX: For thus says the Lord of powers: Glean, glean as in a vineyard the remnant of Israel; return like a grape-gatherer to his basket! Some take these words in a good sense, others in a bad. In the good sense: 'When Jerusalem has been laid waste, let the remnant be saved'. …
7:11: Has this house — or my house —, in which my name has been called upon, become a den of robbers in your eyes? I, I am, I have seen, says the Lord. From this passage, I think, was taken what is in the Gospel: It is written: My Father's house shall be called a house of prayer; but you have made it a den of robbers, or, as is written in another Gospel, a house of trade. …
7:12: Go to my place in Shiloh, where my name dwelt from the beginning, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel! From the past he teaches the present, and to those who say: the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord and who rejoice in the gleam of a costly house he recalls the history of Shiloh, where the tabernacle of God first was, of which it is written in the psalm: and he rejected the tabernacle of Shiloh, so that, just as that place collapsed into ruins …
7:13: And now, because you have done all these works, says the Lord, and I spoke to you, rising early and speaking, and you did not hear, and I called you and you did not answer, I will do to this house, in which my name has been called upon and in which you have confidence, and to the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I did to Shiloh, and I will cast you out from my face, as I cast out all your brothers, the whole seed of Ephraim. …
7:14: Since, therefore, God called them, rising by night, so that he might free them too from darkness, he threatens them that he will do to the temple in Jerusalem things like those he did to the place Shiloh, where the tabernacle first was, so that like sins may be struck by an equal sentence. …
7:17: Do you not see what these are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? The sons gather wood and the fathers kindle the fire and the women sprinkle fat, to make cakes — or chauonas — for the queen — or the host — of heaven, and to pour libations to strange gods and to provoke me to anger. Is it me they provoke to anger? says the Lord, is it not themselves, to the confusion of their own face? 'Do you wish,' he says, 'to hear, prophet, why I said to you: do not pray for this people? …
7:2: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying: Stand in the gate of the house of the Lord and proclaim — or read — there this word, and say: Hear the word of the Lord, all Judah, you who enter by these gates to worship the Lord! This is not found in the edition of the Seventy, but has been added from Theodotion out of the Hebrew. …
7:20: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, my fury and my indignation is kindled — or has dripped — upon this place, upon men and upon beasts and upon the trees of the region and upon the fruits of the earth, and it will be set alight and will not be quenched. He who had said above: Is it me they provoke to anger?, how does he now say: Behold, my fury and my indignation has dripped upon this place? …
7:21: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Add your burnt offerings to your victims and eat flesh, for I did not speak with your fathers, and I did not command them on the day that I led them out of the land of Egypt, concerning the matter of burnt offerings and victims, but this word I commanded them, saying: Hear my voice, and I will be your God and you will be my people, and walk in every way that I have commanded you, that it may be well with you. …
7:24: And they did not hear nor incline their ear, but they went off in the wills — or desires — and the depravity of their evil heart, and they became backward and not forward, from the day on which their fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day. …
7:25: And I sent to you my servants, the prophets, by day, rising at daybreak and sending; and they did not hear me nor incline their ear, but they hardened their neck and wrought worse than their fathers. Just, therefore, is the wrath of the Lord, which has been kindled and has dripped upon a contemptuous and stiff-necked people that refuses to hear the words of God. But how God sends the prophets either by night or at daybreak and by day, we have said above.
7:27: And you will speak to them all these words, and they will not hear you; and you will call them, and they will not answer you. And you will say to them: This is the nation that has not heard the voice of the Lord its God nor received discipline; faith has perished and has been taken away from their mouth. …
7:29: Shear your hair and cast it away, and take up in the open — or upon the lips — a lament, for the Lord has cast off and forsaken the generation of his fury. We read that Job too, on hearing of the death of his sons and daughters, sheared his hair, and among the ancients this was the custom of all who mourned, to shear the locks; but now, on the contrary, to let the hair grow long is the sign of mourning. …
7:3: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Make good — or direct — your ways and your pursuits — or your devices — and I will dwell with you in this place or I will make you dwell in this place. The most merciful physician desires to heal the wounded with every remedy. But when he says: make good or correct your ways, he shows that they are perverse and have nothing good in them. …
7:30: For the sons of Judah have done evil in my sight, says the Lord; they have set their stumbling blocks in the house in which my name has been called upon, to pollute it, and they have built the high places — or the altar — of Topheth, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters with fire, which I did not command nor think of in my heart. That the sons of Judah set up a statue of Baal in the temple of God we learn at the beginning of Ezekiel. …
7:32: Therefore, behold, the days will come, says the Lord, and it will no longer be called Topheth and the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of killing, and they will bury in Topheth because there is no room. And the carcasses of this people will be food for the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, and there will be none to drive them away. …
7:34: And I will make to cease from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, and the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; for the land will be in desolation. …
7:4: Do not trust in lying words, saying: The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord it is! For if you direct well — or direct — your ways and your pursuits, if you execute judgment between a man and his neighbor, if you do not practice false accusation against the stranger and the orphan and the widow — or do not oppress them — and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not walk after strange gods to your own harm, I will dwell with you — or I will make you dwell — in this place, …
7:5: Then he adds: 'if you make your ways straight, and your thought does not go off after error, and you follow righteousness and do not commit evil, and do not shed innocent blood by scandalizing every simple person, and do not walk after strange gods by worshipping perverse doctrines which you have feigned out of your own heart to your own harm, then either I will dwell with you in this place, which you call the temple of God, and in the land which I gave to your fathers, namely the apostles and apostolic men, or at …
7:8: Behold, you trust in words of falsehood — or lying words —, which will not profit you: to steal, to kill, to commit adultery, to swear falsely, to pour libations to the Baals, and to go after strange gods whom you do not know. And you came and stood before me in this house, in which my name has been called upon, and you said: We are delivered — or we have ceased — because we have done all these abominations. The sins that follow show that they have confidence in the temple in vain. …
8:1: At that time, says the Lord, they shall cast out the bones of the king of Judah and the bones of his princes and the bones of the priests and the bones of the prophets and the bones of those who dwelt in Jerusalem, from their graves. And they shall spread them out to the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven, which they have loved and which they have served and after which they have walked and which they have sought and worshiped. …
8:10: Therefore I will give their women — or wives — to strangers, their fields to heirs, because from the least to the greatest all are devoted to avarice, from the prophet to the priest all practice falsehood — or iniquity —. And they healed the breaking of the daughter of my people to ignominy, saying: Peace, peace, when there was not peace. They received the wages of their works, so that those who cast away the word of the Lord were themselves cast away by him. …
8:12: Were they confounded, because they committed abomination? Nay rather, they were not confounded with confusion, and they did not know how to blush. This is to be read Erōtēmatikōs [as a question], so that the sense is: 'Did they blush in their crimes, did they understand the abominations which they wrought?' 'By no means; but they burst out into such madness that they neither desired to amend their vices through confusion nor to confess their crimes in hope of pardon'.
8:13: Gathering I will gather them, says the Lord; there is no grape on the vines and there are no figs on the fig tree; the leaf has fallen, and I have given them things that have passed by. What the time of visitation is, in which the transgressors shall collapse, he teaches more plainly, saying: 'Gathering I will gather them' — no doubt in Jerusalem —, 'so that they may be besieged by the Chaldeans for a long time and endure the evils of famine. …
8:14: Why do we sit still? Come together, and let us enter the fortified city — or the fortified cities — and let us be silent there — or let us be cast out there —, for our Lord has cast us off — or has made us silent — and has given us water of gall to drink; for we have sinned against the Lord. We waited for peace, and there was no good, for a time of healing, and behold, dread. …
8:16: From Dan was heard the snorting of his horses, at the sound of the neighings of his fighters — or of his cavalry — the whole land was shaken; and they came and devoured — or and they will come and will devour — the land and its fullness, the city and its inhabitants. So the people did not say, as the Seventy translated above: let us enter the fortified cities, but: the fortified city, so as to signify Jerusalem. And indeed he now also adds: the city and its inhabitants. …
8:17: For behold, I will send among you serpents, basilisks — or most wicked or, as the Seventy translated, deadly —, for which there is no charm; and they shall bite you, says the Lord, incurably, with the pain of your failing heart. …
8:18: My pain is above pain, within me my heart is mourning. For this, as we said above, the Seventy joined what is said to the preceding sentence, so as to put: and they shall bite you, says the Lord, incurably, with the pain of your failing heart. But in the Hebrew there is not so much 'pain', which in Greek is called odynē, as meidiama, which we can translate as the 'grimace' of a mouth contracted by pain and having the likeness of a smile. …
8:19: Is the Lord not in Zion, or is her king not in her? Either the Lord himself is the king, or else 'Lord' refers to the Father, 'king' to the Son, according to that which is written under the name of Solomon: O God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the son of the king. But why the voice of crying is in Jerusalem and the crying itself comes from a land far off, the cause is manifest: because the Lord is not in her and her king has withdrawn from her.
8:20: The harvest is past, the summer is ended; and we are not saved. Again the people speaks, which was shut up in Jerusalem by a long siege, saying that the seasons have changed and the circle of the year has rolled round, and all their hope has been made void and has passed away.
8:21: Over the breaking of the daughter of my people I am broken and saddened, astonishment has taken hold of me. God answers that in the affliction of Jerusalem he himself appears afflicted, and, after the likeness of a man, he is broken by astonishment.
8:22: Is there no resin in Gilead, or is there no physician there? Why then has the scar of the daughter of my people not closed over? Not only in the present passage, but also in many other testimonies of the Scriptures we find the resin of Gilead put for repentance and medicine; and we find that God now wonders why the wounds of Jerusalem have by no means been healed and the scars have not yet drawn over the skin, because there are no prophets or priests by whose medicine they ought to be healed.
8:5: Why then has this people in Jerusalem turned away with a contentious turning away? They have laid hold of falsehood and they would not return? 'The more I,' he says, 'called them to repentance, the more they withdrew from me, not so much from eagerness to sin as from eagerness to overcome me. …
8:7: The kite in the heaven has known its time; the turtledove and the swallow and the stork have kept the time of their coming; but my people has not known the judgment of the Lord. For 'kite', which Symmachus translated, the Seventy and Theodotion put the Hebrew word itself, 'asida', Aquila 'herodiona' [heron]. And again for 'swallow' Symmachus translated 'cicada', which in Hebrew is called 'sis'. …
8:8: How do you say: We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us? Truly the lying pen of the scribes has wrought falsehood. He speaks to the scribes and Pharisees, who boast of their knowledge of the law and, writing, write iniquity. And as for what he says:
8:9: The wise are confounded, terrified and taken, it is not that those who do these things are wise, but he calls them wise so that they may be condemned by their own judgment and, on the contrary, their wisdom may be proved to be folly, as Paul says: you who teach another, do you not teach yourself? And because they have cast away the word of the Lord, therefore there is no wisdom in them. In vain, then, do they boast of knowledge of the law who destroy their teaching by their works.
9:10: Upon the mountains I will take up — or take up — weeping and lamentation, and over the beautiful places — or the paths — of the desert a wailing, because they are burned up — or they have failed — because there is no man — or human being — passing through. And they have not heard the voice of the possessor — or of substance —; from the bird of the heaven to the beasts they have migrated and withdrawn. …
9:11: And I will give Jerusalem into heaps of sand — or into exile — and into lairs of dragons, and the cities of Judah I will give into desolation, because there is no inhabitant. When churchmen and all the teachers have failed, then Jerusalem is given into exile or into heaps of sand, so that heretical speech prevails in her and she is made a lair of dragons and her cities are reduced to a wilderness, and there is in her no dwelling of the divine word and of him who says: I will dwell and walk among them, and I will …
9:12: Who is the wise man who may understand this, and to whom the word of the mouth of the Lord may come, and who may declare it: why the land has perished and is burned up like a desert, because there is none who passes through? And the Lord said: Because they have forsaken my law, which I gave them, and have not heard my voice and have not walked in it, and have gone after the perversity of their heart and after the Baals, whom they learned from their fathers. …
9:13: And he brings in the Lord answering and giving the reasons: because they had forsaken his law, which he had given them, and had not heard his voice nor done what had been commanded, but had gone after the perversity of their heart. Therefore we must trust not in our own will but in the Lord; for the heart in men is perverse, and from our heart come forth the worst thoughts. And after the Baals, he says, they have gone, whom they learned from their fathers. …
9:15: Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will feed them, this people, with wormwood — or with distresses — and I will give them water of gall for drink, and I will scatter them among the nations which neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them until they are consumed. …
9:19: How are we laid waste and confounded exceedingly? Because we have forsaken the land, for our tents have been thrown down — or we have cast away —. This is the voice of those lamenting Zion: how are we laid waste and confounded exceedingly? And at once they answer themselves and set out the causes of the devastation, saying: because we have forsaken the land through our own fault and sin, and our tents have been thrown down, which they once possessed as if passing by. …
9:2: For they are all adulterers, an assembly of transgressors, and they have stretched out their tongue like a bow of falsehood and not of truth; they have grown strong in the land, for they have gone forth from evil to evil, and they have not known me, says the Lord. Sinners pass from evil to evil when they exchange idol for idol and go over from sins to sins, or at any rate pass from the evil of the siege to captivity. …
9:20: Hear therefore, O women, the word of the Lord, and let your ear take up the speech of his mouth, and teach your daughters lamentation, and each woman her neighbor wailing, for death has come up through our windows, it has entered our houses, to destroy the little ones from outside, the young men from the streets! …
9:21: These are the windows of which Jeremiah also says: Death has entered through our windows; for the enemies desire to enter through all our senses, and to take the city of a good conscience, and to run about through our fortifications, and to destroy the houses which we have built for ourselves by good works. And they do all things entering through the windows like a thief, for they do not enter openly, that they may shoot in the dark at the upright of heart.
9:22: Speak: Thus says the Lord: And the carcass of man shall fall — or the corpses of men — like dung upon the face of the region — or of the field — and like hay behind the back of the reaper, and there is none who gathers. The Hebrew word that is written with three letters, 'daleth, beth, res' — for it has no vowels in the middle —, if it is read, according to the context and the judgment of the reader, as 'dabar', means 'word'; if as 'deber', 'death'; if as 'dabber', 'speak'. …
9:23: Thus says the Lord: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, and let not the strong man glory in his strength, and let not the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in this: to know — or to understand — and to know me, that I am the Lord, who do mercy and judgment and righteousness on the earth! For these things please me — or for in these is my will —, says the Lord. …
9:25: Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will visit upon everyone who have the foreskin circumcised, upon Egypt and upon Judah and upon Edom and upon the sons of Ammon and upon Moab and upon all who are shorn about the hair, dwelling in the desert; for all the nations have the foreskin, but all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart. …
9:4: Let each one guard himself from his neighbor, and let him not have confidence in any brother of his, for every brother supplants with supplanting, and every friend walks deceitfully, and a man will mock his brother, and they will not speak the truth; for their tongue has learned to speak falsehood — or for they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood —. They have labored to act wickedly — or they have acted wickedly and have not ceased, so as to be converted —. …
9:6: And as for what follows: your dwelling is in the midst of deceit, in deceit, the word is properly directed to the prophet, that he dwells in the midst of a lying people — or, as the Seventy translated: usury upon usury and deceit upon deceit — and that they daily increase their crimes and by no means repent of their former deed, but heap new crimes upon past ones; doing these things, they act with all eagerness so as not to know the Lord, who commanded that these things should not be done.
9:7: Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will melt — or I will test by fire — and try them; for what else shall I do in the face of the daughter of my people? Or for I will act in the face of the wickedness of the daughter of my people. …
9:8: Their tongue is a wounding arrow, it has spoken deceit; with his mouth he speaks peace with his friend and secretly lays snares for him. Shall I not visit upon these things, says the Lord, or on such a nation shall my soul not take vengeance? Every heretic who wounds the hearts of his hearers, of those who do not know what is written: keep your heart with all watchfulness, possesses a wounding arrow and speaks in deceit, and while with his mouth he promises peace to his neighbor, he secretly sets snares.
9:9: As for the following verses, in which he says: shall I not visit upon these things, says the Lord, or on such a nation shall my soul not take vengeance? He makes frequent use of them in this prophet, so that, when he has enumerated the evil works one by one, he infers that he does justly what he does.
